title.narrative: Response to the Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals and Host Community (HC) (EA/2023)

description.narrative:
After 6 years following the the exodus of Rohingya from Myanmar, more than 1 million refugees are still living in temporary settlements spread across 34 congested camps in Cox’s Bazar District, Bangladesh. In their current circumstances, they lack formal legal status, face extreme restrictions on movement and are not permitted to legally work. The refugee influx overwhelmed the existing response capacity and put immense strain on infrastructure, services, resources and the local environment, and the extreme level of humanitarian needs has not decreased. The Government of Bangladesh and local communities have supported the refugees to the best of their ability, but solidarity has been strained, especially in recent years given the global shift in funding to new conflicts and crises.
Caritas Bangladesh (CB) was one of the first humanitarian actors to respond in 2017, and despite decreasing funding, has been continuously responding to the emergency needs of Rohingya refugees since then through food and NFI distributions, shelter construction, settlement planning and upgrading, provision of WASH facilities, and community-based protection for families and children. Over the last 6 years Caritas Bangladesh has reached well over a 1 million people.
This contribution will go towards CB's emergency appeal (EA) for 2023 and focus on key areas which have not been funded. Activities for this funding include the distribution of solar lamps, health and hygiene/menstrual kits and the repair and maintenance of camp centres.
